title: Data Manager: inspect, prune and archive a real example safely
description: Inspect registered and unregistered files, cancel and confirm an exact crop cleanup, then move a private example project with its archive records.
objectives: Find Data manager under Help and inspect actual project usage.
Read the exact deletion plan, kept reasons and complete confirmation list.
Distinguish irreversible cleanup from archiving and verify Cancel preserves files.
Rescan the archive and retain its manifest, origin ledger and original backup.
prerequisite: Follow External Masks to obtain the genuine two-field example with 103 measured objects and saved figures. This recording uses an isolated, byte-verified copy of that completed project; its original absolute registry paths resolve only to the disposable copy inside the recording process. All 131 original files remain unchanged. Data Manager has no separate dataset download, live image preview, Plot control or AI panel. Its displayed sizes count bytes on disk, not scientific quality. Cleanup removes 103 PNG crops and their format JSON from the copy only, retains the measured database and recorded recipe, and does not demonstrate regeneration. Archiving moves the remaining project; it is not a backup or a guarantee that every historical absolute path has been rewritten. External resource logs stay outside this whole-project move.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Data manager. This shared tool manages project files; it does not run image analysis. We use a disposable copy of the real External Masks example, including its measurements and saved figures. Keep an independent backup before trying cleanup yourself.

Choose project selects the project root. Usage shows about ninety-one megabytes in one hundred twenty-nine files after scanning. Registered and Unregistered are different: files can exist without a registry record. Folder-based category labels are estimates, not proof of the files' scientific content.

On Prune, choose which kinds to consider. A selected switch does not itself authorize deletion. Leave measurement databases and model weights unchecked here, then choose Show what can be deleted. Read both the proposed files and the reasons other artifacts are kept.

This plan contains only the data crop folder: one hundred three object images and one format file, not one hundred four cells. It proposes freeing about three point four megabytes. Get it back by names Measure, but regeneration still requires the original inputs, settings and suitable software.

Delete opens a second confirmation with the actual file list. It cannot be undone. Resize the dialog and scroll through the paths before acknowledging them. The final Delete button starts disabled; enabling the acknowledgment is a separate action from deleting anything.

The acknowledgment enables Delete. Turning it off disables Delete again. In this first demonstration we choose Cancel instead, and every project file remains unchanged. Cancel is the correct choice whenever the paths, file counts or expected recovery procedure are uncertain.

We reopen the same verified plan and confirm deletion only on our disposable copy. The result reports three point four megabytes freed in one hundred four files. All twenty-four other non-registry files remain byte-identical, including the measurement database and saved figures.

The automatic rescan now reports one registered artifact missing from disk: the deliberately removed crop folder. Its recipe remains in the registry with cleanup metadata. That record is not an undo buffer, and we have not rerun Measure to regenerate the crops.

Archive is different: it moves the remaining project. Choose an empty destination outside the source, then Show what would move. After cleanup, this plan contains twenty-five files totaling about eighty-eight megabytes. Read the source and destination carefully; this screen plans the whole project.

Move asks for confirmation, with No selected by default. First we choose No and verify that the source remains unchanged and the destination empty. A plan and a cancelled confirmation move nothing. Do not treat the archive destination as an extra backup copy.

We confirm Yes only for this private example. The remaining files move to the destination. A manifest is written there and an archive log remains at the origin. The original project used to create our disposable copy stays completely unchanged.

Choose the destination as the project and scan again. The archived measurement database is registered at its new path, and every non-registry file matches its pre-move bytes. The extra manifest explains the new file count. Historical records and external logs are not automatically rewritten or relocated.

For Python automation, spacr.data_manager exposes scan_project, plan_prune, prune, plan_archive and archive. Inspect the plan before supplying its confirmation token. For browsing measurements use Database Browser; for a readable project summary use Report. Keep the separate backup and archive records together with your research documentation.
